Study Guide for Unit 1

1. Hypothesis Testing

Null hypothesis:

\[ H_0: \text{parameter} = \text{hypothesized value} \]

Alternative hypotheses:

Research question Alternative Test
Greater than (H_a: \(\text{parameter}\) > \(\text{value}\)) Right-tailed
Less than (H_a: \(\text{parameter}\) < \(\text{value}\)) Left-tailed
Different from (H_a: \(\text{parameter}\) \(\ne\) \(\text{value}\)) Two-tailed
Decision Using a P-Value
  • If (\(p \le \alpha\)), reject (\(H_0\)).
  • If (\(p > \alpha\)), fail to reject (\(H_0\)).

2. One-Sample (\(z\)) Test for a Mean

Use when the population standard deviation (\(\sigma\)) is known.

Test Statistic

\[ z=\frac{\bar{x}-\mu_0}{\sigma/\sqrt{n}} \]

where:

  • \(\bar{x}\) = sample mean
  • \(\mu_0\) = hypothesized population mean
  • \(\sigma\) = population standard deviation
  • \(n\) = sample size
z <- (xbar - mu0) / (sigma / sqrt(n))
P-Value
# Left-tailed
pnorm(z)

# Right-tailed
1 - pnorm(z)

# Two-tailed
2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z)))
Critical Values
# Left-tailed
qnorm(alpha)

# Right-tailed
qnorm(1 - alpha)

# Two-tailed
qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)

3. One-Sample (t) Test for a Mean

Use when the population standard deviation is unknown and \(s\) is used instead.

Test Statistic

\[ t=\frac{\bar{x}-\mu_0}{s/\sqrt{n}} \]

Degrees of Freedom

\[ df=n-1 \]

df <- n - 1

t_stat <- (xbar - mu0) / (s / sqrt(n))
P-Value
# Left-tailed
pt(t_stat, df)

# Right-tailed
1 - pt(t_stat, df)
pt(t_stat, df, lower.tail = FALSE)

# Two-tailed
2 * pt(-abs(t_stat), df)
Critical Values
# Left-tailed
qt(alpha, df)

# Right-tailed
qt(1 - alpha, df)
qt(alpha, df, lower.tail = FALSE)

# Two-tailed
qt(1 - alpha / 2, df)

4. Confidence Interval for a Population Mean

When \(\sigma\) Is Known

\[ \bar{x}\pm z_{\alpha/2}\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}} \]

z_critical <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)

margin_error <- z_critical * sigma / sqrt(n)

lower <- xbar - margin_error
upper <- xbar + margin_error
When \(\sigma\) Is Unknown

\[ \bar{x}\pm t_{\alpha/2,df}\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} \]

with:

\[ df=n-1 \]

df <- n - 1

t_critical <- qt(1 - alpha / 2, df)

margin_error <- t_critical * s / sqrt(n)

lower <- xbar - margin_error
upper <- xbar + margin_error

c(lower = lower, upper = upper)
CI for a Two-Tailed Test

For:

\[ H_0:\mu=\mu_0 \]

  • If \(\mu_0\) is inside the confidence interval, fail to reject \(H_0\).
  • If \(\mu_0\) is outside the confidence interval, reject \(H_0\).

5. One-Proportion \(z\) Test

Use when testing a population proportion.

Sample Proportion

\[ \hat{p}=\frac{x}{n} \]

p_hat <- x / n

where \(x\) is the number with the characteristic of interest.

Check the Conditions

Both should be at least 5:

\[ np_0\ge5 \]

\[ n(1-p_0)\ge5 \]

n * p0
n * (1 - p0)
Test Statistic

\[ z= \frac{\hat{p}-p_0} {\sqrt{\frac{p_0(1-p_0)}{n}}} \]

z <- (p_hat - p0) /
     sqrt(p0 * (1 - p0) / n)

Then use the same pnorm() commands as any other \(z\) test:

# Left-tailed
pnorm(z)

# Right-tailed
1 - pnorm(z)
pnorm(z, lower.tail = FALSE)

# Two-tailed
2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z)))

6. Chi-Square Test for a Population Variance

Use when testing a population variance or standard deviation.

If standard deviations are given, convert them to variance:

\[ s^2=(s)^2 \]

\[ \sigma_0^2=(\sigma_0)^2 \]

s^2
sigma0^2
Test Statistic

\[ \chi^2= \frac{(n-1)s^2}{\sigma_0^2} \]

Degrees of Freedom

\[ df=n-1 \]

df <- n - 1

chi_square <- (n - 1) * s^2 / sigma0^2
Critical Values
# Left-tailed
qchisq(alpha, df)

# Right-tailed
qchisq(1 - alpha, df)
qchisq(alpha, df, lower.tail = FALSE)

# Two-tailed
lower <- qchisq(alpha / 2, df)
upper <- qchisq(1 - alpha / 2, df)
P-Values
# Left-tailed
pchisq(chi_square, df)

# Right-tailed
1 - pchisq(chi_square, df)
pchisq(chi_square, df, lower.tail = FALSE)

Quick Reference

Problem Formula / R
Sample proportion p_hat <- x / n
Mean (z) statistic z <- (xbar - mu0) / (sigma / sqrt(n))
Mean (t) statistic t_stat <- (xbar - mu0) / (s / sqrt(n))
Proportion (z) statistic z <- (p_hat - p0) / sqrt(p0*(1-p0)/n)
Chi-square statistic chi_square <- (n - 1) * s^2 / sigma0^2
Degrees of freedom df <- n - 1
Distribution Critical Value
(starts with q)		 P-Value
(starts with p)
z qnorm() pnorm()
t qt() pt()
chi-squared qchisq() pchisq()
